objective: Define the reusable graduation baseline for external runtimes that want to become interchangeable daily-driver engines under InfRing.

proof_accounting.rule: External-engine mediated work proves InfRing can govern runtime engines through Gateway. It does not prove native InfRing intelligence.

secondary_eval_samples.rule: Secondary samples may receive deterministic continuity/projection evidence without becoming promotion-eligible. Promotion still requires the full golden-pair baseline and live adapter evidence.

secondary_readiness_artifacts.rule: Diagnostic only; this artifact may refine next actions but must not count as daily-driver promotion evidence.

commands.note: Preferred when Volta is already installed because it avoids changing global system Node unexpectedly.

after_runtime_ready: Start the OpenClaw Gateway/socket service from the detected reference checkout or configured command.
Only then run live Gateway-mediated adapter evidence.

secondary_promotion_plan_artifact.rule: Secondary runtimes must expose a compact ordered promotion plan before operators spend live usage, install dependencies, or treat readiness as promotion.

graduation_rule.summary: A non-baseline runtime cannot be promoted as reliable, production-ready, baseline-covered, golden-pair-equivalent, or daily-driver-candidate until it proves the same practical primitives as the Codex/Claude golden pair.

baseline_primitives.description: Runtime has a registry row and stable canonical engine id.
Runtime declares an adapter implementation path behind Gateway.
Runtime exposes model/provider catalog metadata without Shell-owned inference.
Runtime receives enough InfRing context to preserve multi-turn continuity.
Runtime has live InfRing-mediated adapter evidence, not only native CLI or fixture proof.
Runtime can complete useful live work through the Agent Runtime route.
Runtime participates in reusable real-work replay evidence.
Runtime proves approval pause, bounded projection, receipt, transcript persistence, context reload, artifact effect, and activity trace.
Runtime maps mutation attempts into Gateway-owned approval pause instead of silent failure.
Runtime preserves active user steering through Gateway without duplicate chat bubbles, lost steering text, or Shell-owned runtime authority.
Runtime returns durable receipts for approved effects and user decisions.
Runtime emits bounded user-facing activity/decision trace projections.
Runtime has structured transport evidence or an explicit bounded-envelope compatibility posture.
Runtime has a declared migration path away from prompt-text compatibility where possible.
Runtime surfaces quota, auth, rate-limit, network, and missing-runtime failures as visible chat outcomes.

forbidden_shortcuts: Promoting a runtime from native CLI success without InfRing-mediated Gateway proof.
Counting external-engine mediated work as native InfRing intelligence proof.
Adding Shell-owned inference to compensate for missing adapter/runtime primitives.
Treating a candidate native transport surface as upstream live typed acceptance without a disposable live acceptance probe.
